terms.meaning: the red style used for errors or serious warnings

sections.name: File setup, ToastProps (part 1)
sections.title: Message area and frame styling
sections.what: Defines where messages appear on screen and how the message frame looks, in a normal style and a red destructive style.
sections.why: Likely reason: a standard notice layout reused by the whole app.

sections.name: File setup, ToastProps (part 2)
sections.title: Action, close, title and text parts
sections.what: Defines the optional action button, the close X button, and the title and description text inside a message.
sections.why: Likely reason: these parts are put together by the toaster to build each message.
sections.watch_out: The close button stays invisible until hovered or focused, so it can be hard to find on touch screens.

sections.name: ToastActionElement
sections.title: Message type and export list
sections.what: Declares the type for the optional action button and lists everything other files can import from this file.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets other files type the action they pass in.
sections.watch_out: Renaming an export breaks the toaster and any other file that imports it.

summary: The visual parts of a popup message: the screen area, the message frame, the title and text, an optional action button, and a close button.
purpose: Shows short messages such as success or error notices that disappear by themselves.
why: Likely reason: a standard notice kit used by the toaster and the toast hook. The reason for the destructive style is not stated.
how: Defines the screen area, which sits at the top on phones and at the bottom right on larger screens. Defines the message frame with a normal look and a red destructive look. Also defines the optional action button, the close button, and the title and text parts. Some class text is cut off in the sample.
inputs: Props for each part, a variant choice, and the usual message props.
risks: The close button is invisible until it is hovered or focused, which can be hard to find on touch screens. Parts of the sample were cut, so some styling is unverified.
debug: If messages do not appear, check that the toaster is on the page. If a message looks wrong, check its variant.
